scenes.text: The museum closes in ten minutes. You stand outside the staff entrance, earpiece in, pulse hammering. Your fence has a buyer for the Kohinoor replica — but your partner just went dark.

choices.text: Wait five more minutes for your partner

scenes.text: The service corridor is empty. Motion sensors sweep every eight seconds. You count under your breath — seven, eight. Go.
A shadow rounds the corner — it's Mira, your partner. Her jacket is torn. 'Guards changed shift early,' she whispers. 'We have a problem.'

choices.text: Adapt the plan — go through the roof

scenes.text: You turn for the exit — only to find two guards blocking it. They haven't seen you yet. You back into the supply room. There is only one other way out: through the vault corridor.

choices.text: Hide and wait for a shift change

scenes.text: The display case is locked with a biometric seal. Your portable spoofer takes thirty seconds it doesn't have. Footsteps in the hall.

choices.text: Use the spoofer and risk being caught

scenes.text: The junction box sparks open. All cameras on floor two go dark. Six minutes until the security room notices the outage.

choices.text: Head straight to the display room

scenes.text: The roof hatch is unlocked — almost suspiciously so. Mira mouths 'trap?' You shrug and go up. The city glitters below. The skylight to the display room is three metres away.
An hour passes. The supply room is suffocating. Dawn light threads under the door. Shift change — but now a detective is with the guards.
The spoofer clicks. The case hisses open. Replica in hand — cold, heavy, perfect. Twenty-eight seconds left. Then the alarms scream.

choices.text: Hide the replica and blend in with staff

scenes.text: Glass explodes. You snatch the replica and sprint. Every alarm in the building ignites. You have thirty seconds before the exits lock.
A guard is posted at the north stairwell — but he's asleep, chin on chest. You slip past without a sound.
Hands up. The detective is almost sympathetic. 'We've been watching you for six months,' she says. The replica was a decoy. You were the test.
The getaway bike idles in the alley. You drop into the seat, the replica strapped to your chest. The city swallows you whole. The fence will be very pleased.
You pull on a visitor lanyard and walk calmly toward the exit with the tour group. The guards scan faces. They wave you through. Outside, the night air tastes like freedom.
The loading dock is a dead end. Shutter doors sealed. You press against the wall as flashlights sweep the space. There is nowhere left to go.
